answer:
**Result: Pearson r = 0.31 (r = 0.3136, n = 19,942 protein-coding genes), using mean log2(CPM+1) across all 723 samples vs gene Length.**

Definition of the primary answer (as approved): gene_biotype == "protein_coding" exactly; expression = mean over all 723 samples of log2(CPM+1), CPM = per-sample count / sample column total × 10⁶; Pearson correlation against the metadata `Length` column. Rows/columns were verified element-wise aligned before computing.

**Sensitivity table (definitional dependence is visible — primary is row 1):**

| Definition | n | Pearson r |
|---|---|---|
| **PRIMARY: mean(log2(CPM+1)), exact PC filter, all genes** | 19,942 | **0.3136** |
| log2(mean CPM + 1), exact PC | 19,942 | 0.3167 |
| raw mean counts (all genes), exact PC | 19,942 | 0.0504 |
| raw mean counts (nonzero-expression genes only), exact PC | 19,297 | 0.0460 |
| mean(log2(CPM+1)), substring PC filter | 19,954 | 0.3134 |
| mean(log2(CPM+1)), exact PC, all-zero genes dropped | 19,297 | 0.2918 |
| raw mean counts (nonzero), substring PC filter | 19,309 | 0.0460 |
| mean(log2(CPM+1)), exact PC, Length==8 gene dropped | 19,942 | 0.3136 (unchanged) |
| mean of per-sample Pearson r (raw counts), exact PC | 19,942 genes × 723 samples | 0.0482 (median per-sample r = 0.0490) |

**Key diagnostics and observations:**
- **Length = 8 gene identified, not silently deleted:** it is **TRDD1** (biotype TR_D_gene, Chr 14) — a T-cell receptor delta diversity gene, a genuine 8-bp germline gene segment. It is *not* in the protein-coding set (protein-coding Length range is 51–118,976, median 4,336), so it has zero effect on the primary result (r unchanged when dropped anyway).
- The correlation is strongly definition-dependent: length-normalized/log metrics give r ≈ 0.29–0.32 (consistent with the known positive length–expression relationship in RNA-seq), while **raw mean counts give r ≈ 0.05** — because unnormalized count means retain library-size and count-variance artifacts that mask the length effect; the log-CPM metric is the appropriate one on this raw-scale data (per-sample totals vary ~3.8M–21.7M).
- Substring vs exact biotype filter changes n by only 12 genes (19,954 vs 19,942) and r by 0.0002 — negligible.
- Spearman ρ = 0.44 on the primary definition (monotonic relationship slightly stronger than linear).
- Execution evidence: script at `analysis/length_expression_correlation.py`, results table at `analysis/results_correlation.csv`; all assertions on alignment passed.

**Limitations:** Length semantics (transcript/exonic vs genomic span) are undocumented; symbol-level aggregation may merge paralogs/multiple transcripts; "batch-corrected" matrix remains on integer raw-count scale; expression averaged over all samples ignores cell-type/batch structure (per-sample correlation averaging, r ≈ 0.05, confirms raw counts are unsuitable without normalization).

payload.final_answer: Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.31 (r = 0.3136, n = 19,942 protein-coding genes) between gene length and gene expression, where expression is the mean across all 723 samples of log2(CPM+1). The result is definition-dependent: raw mean counts yield r ≈ 0.05, log-normalized metrics yield r ≈ 0.29-0.32.
payload.primary_definition: mean log2(CPM+1) across 723 samples, exact protein_coding filter
